# targets Pipeline Documentation

This document describes the `targets` pipeline for the IPBES BM Fact Checker project.

**Note: this document predates the reporting/explorer layer and is stale in
that respect** — it does not describe the `claim_work_pairs` →
`claim_units` → `claim_scores_by_claim` chain, or the
downstream `nli_overview_data`, `nli_overview_figures`, `nli_bm_explorer_html`,
`reports_project`, and `report_fact_checker` targets, all of which exist and run
today. See `_targets.R` and [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)'s R-files table for the
current, authoritative target list.

## Overview

The pipeline fetches IPBES assessment data from the [IPBES Linked Open Data (LOD)](https://github.com/IPBES-Data/IPBES_LOD) repository in RDF/Turtle format, queries the assessments via SPARQL, and produces per-assessment Parquet datasets for refs, sections, key-messages, Zotero items, OpenAlex works, snowball results, and NLI alignment scores.

The **active scoring approach** is NLI (`nli_scores_by_claim` / `claim_scores_by_claim`): each citing work is classified as SUPPORTS / REFUTES / NOT_ENOUGH_INFO against its partition's Background Message using a zero-shot `bge-m3-zeroshot-v2.0-c` NLI model served on RunPod (see [external/runpod/docker/nli-runpod/](external/runpod/docker/nli-runpod/) and [TD_BM_NLI_approach.qmd](TD_BM_NLI_approach.html)) — `deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0` was the original model, now retired.

**Phase 2 LLM verification** (`llm_verification_parquet`) reviews whichever slice of NLI scores each config's `nli_labels`/`nli_certainty` fields select (currently `REFUTES` + `SUPPORTS`, both `certain`, on every shipped config — ~79k of 3.5M scored pairs), one `ellmer::chat_openrouter()` call per `(claim, work)` pair — every routed pair is reviewed, none filtered, but each is tagged `direct_evidence_match` by `llm_candidate_scope_parquet` (via IPBES's own sub-chapter evidence references; a former `subset: "default"` candidate-narrowing filter was retired here since it only reduced routed pairs by ~14%, not worth the lost review coverage) — see [TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.qmd](TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.html) for the design and [R/build_llm_verification_parquet.R](R/build_llm_verification_parquet.R)/[R/build_llm_candidate_scope_parquet.R](R/build_llm_candidate_scope_parquet.R) for the implementation. The earlier truth/citing-document LLM design it replaced (`prompts_truth_parquet` → `prompts_citing_parquet` → `alignement_scores_parquet`) has been removed; see [TD_LLM_approach.qmd](TD_LLM_approach.html) for that record.

Fuseki startup and shutdown are handled inside the parquet builders rather than as separate targets. When `sparql_url: fuseki`, each builder boots an in-memory Fuseki, POSTs the TTL into the named graph `http://ontology.ipbes.net/report/<id>` via the Graph Store Protocol, runs its query, and tears Fuseki down.

## Running the Pipeline

The work is split across **four** `targets` projects, declared in
`_targets.yaml`. Each has its own script and its own store, so rendering a
report cannot reach a target that spends GPU time or API credit — a guarantee
that used to rest on remembering `shortcut = TRUE`.

| Project | Script / store | Holds | Credentials |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `_targets.R` / `_targets/` | collection: LOD → refs → zotero → works → snowball → works_citing | `API_openalex` |
| `factcheck` | `_targets_factcheck.R` / `_targets_factcheck/` | citing works → NLI (Phase 1) → LLM verification (Phase 2); **also** the key-paper QA chain and the gold standard | `API_openrouter` |
| `reporting` | `_targets_reporting.R` / `_targets_reporting/` | everything else that renders | **none** |

**There were four projects until 2026-10-05.** A `training` project held key
papers → NLI → LLM → training set → fine-tune → benchmark, plus its own Quarto
project (`input/reports_training/` → `output/reports_training/`) for three QA
reports, because Quarto gives a project exactly one `output-dir`. It was retired
when the model it existed to improve was measured at or below chance at the job
— see [TD_NLI_training.qmd](TD_NLI_training.html) for that record and
`design_notes.md` for the measurements.

Two of its parts were never training and moved into `factcheck`: the **key-paper
QA chain** (do the papers IPBES itself cites as evidence for a Background Message
support it?) and the **gold standard**, which is now the only thing that can test
the decision that retired the rest. With the second Quarto project gone,
`reporting` is once more "everything that renders", and
`report_project_dirs()` is back to a single directory — kept as a one-element
vector so adding a second is adding an element.

The argument below for splitting fact checking from training still holds; it is
simply no longer load-bearing, because there is no second process to separate
from. It is kept because the same reasoning applies to the key-paper chain, which
*is* still a separate process sharing an input.

```r
# The default project is `main` (collection)
targets::tar_make()

# Pick another project for the session...
Sys.setenv(TAR_PROJECT = "factcheck")
targets::tar_make()

# ...or address one directly
targets::tar_make(script = "_targets_reporting.R", store = "_targets_reporting")

# Visualise the dependency graph of the current project
targets::tar_visnetwork()

# Check which targets are outdated
targets::tar_outdated()

# Load a target into your session
targets::tar_load(refs_parquet)
```

`main` deliberately keeps the **original** `_targets/` store. A fresh store
would make every target outdated by definition, and `download_works()`
`unlink()`s its output before refetching while `build_snowball_parquet()` has no
existence check at all — re-running them would cost days of OpenAlex time *and*
produce a different corpus from the one every existing score was computed
against. Targets were therefore *deleted from* `_targets.R` as they moved out.

Each consumer declares the upstream outputs it reads as `format = "file"`
targets **keeping the producing project's target names**, so the moved targets
work verbatim and a genuine upstream change still invalidates downstream through
content hashing.

## Why separate projects

The single DAG mixed several *purposes*. Fact checking is the deliverable:
citing works discovered by the snowball, scored against assessment claims and
routed to an LLM for grounded verification. Training is a side quest: key
papers — the seed references IPBES itself cited — scored and LLM-reviewed
*exhaustively* to distil a fine-tuning set that may or may not produce a model
worth deploying. Reporting renders both. These are not stages of one process;
they are separate processes sharing an input.

| | fact checking (citing works) | key-paper QA |
|---|---|---|
| input | citing works (2,698,608) | key papers (10,432) |
| LLM routing | filtered to `REFUTES`/`SUPPORTS` + certain (7.72% of scored pairs) | **every pair, unconditionally** |
| output | the published finding | a check on whether the finding's own evidence holds |
| cadence | per assessment, ongoing | alongside it, small and bounded |
| cost of being wrong | a wrong claim is published | a sanity check that misleads |

Both now live in `factcheck`, but with entirely separate roots — own premise
tree, own scores tree, own Phase 2 output, own relevance partition — so either
can be run, re-run or deleted without touching the other.

Sharing a DAG meant sharing failure modes that had nothing to do with each
other. Two concrete consequences, both since removed: `nli_scores_qa_data` took
`claim_scores_keypaper` as a **bare, never-read argument** purely so the
training chain would run during a fact-checking build — one line that made
`tar_make(report_fact_checker)` dispatch key-paper GPU work; and rendering a
report could spend money, because `report_fact_checker` transitively depended on
`llm_verification_parquet`. Eleven such bare-argument edges existed solely
because everything was one DAG with mismatched branch shapes.

The split was cheap because the seams were already filesystem paths: 52 of the
then-76 targets (~70%) were `format = "file"` returning parquet roots, and of
the 24 value-returning targets 15 were trivial config reads. Essentially no
*value* crossed a proposed boundary.

**Reporting is its own project rather than part of fact checking** because
reports come from both consumers — the funnel and `QA_NLI_Scores` families from
fact checking, `QA_NLI_Training_Data` and `QA_NLI_Finetuned_Model` from
training. Putting it inside one would split `config.yaml`'s `reports:` block and
`generate_report_wrappers()` across two projects. It also delivers what the
exercise was really about: a reporting project needs no credentials and has
**no path to a paid target** — structurally, not by remembering `shortcut = TRUE`.

### Why collection keeps the original store

This is permanent operating knowledge, not migration trivia. A `targets` store
is the record of what has been built, so a *fresh* store makes every target in
it outdated by definition — regardless of whether its output already exists on
disk. For the collection layer that is not survivable:

| builder | behaviour on a fresh store |
|---|---|
| `download_ttls` | SHA-checked against GitHub, skips if unchanged |
| `download_works` | **`unlink(output_path)` then refetches OpenAlex** |
| `build_snowball_parquet` | **no existence check at all** — the 16 GB job |
| `build_works_citing_parquet` | guard only checks that *upstream* nodes/edges exist |

Re-running those would cost days and real OpenAlex budget, and worse would
produce a *different* corpus from the one every existing score was computed
against. Hence: **never run a bare `tar_make()` on `main`** — always name the
targets.

Relatedly, do not run `tar_prune()` on that store. Orphaned metadata for
removed targets is harmless (`targets` ignores rows for targets not in the
pipeline) and keeps a rollback available. For a `format = "file"` target the
stored value is only the path, so `output/` is not endangered — but there is no
reason to take the risk.

### Cross-project contracts

Consumers cut at the **small consolidated outputs**, never the large
intermediates: `claim_scores_consolidated` is ~300 MB where
`nli_ready_evidence` is 140 GB, and `format = "file"` hashes what it is given.

A **manifest** — a small file of paths, row counts and a digest, tracked instead
of the tree — was considered and rejected. `targets`' guarantee comes from
hashing the actual bytes; a manifest substitutes trust in the producer's
bookkeeping for direct verification, and breaks precisely when it matters: a
partial write, a hand edit or a botched migration leaves the data changed and
the manifest unmoved, so the downstream stays "current" on data that is not.

Two pieces of **shared mutable state that no DAG describes**, and which
therefore have to be remembered:

- `output/nli_scores/.locks/` — the per-host lock directory, shared by both
  scoring projects. Deliberate: one pool, one queue. If both run at once they
  contend for the same hosts, which is the wanted behaviour.
- `output/claim_completion/raw/` and `output/llm_verification/raw*/` — the
  append-only LLM caches. Content-hash keyed, so concurrent use is safe, but
  they are genuine side-channels between projects.

### The feedback loop is a human, not an edge

Training produces a fine-tuned model; if it is good, that model becomes an `nli`
config that **fact checking consumes**. That is a cycle, and a DAG cannot
contain one. After the split it is what it always was: independent pipelines
joined by a person editing `training.finetune` and then `fact_checking.nli`.

Adopting a checkpoint is not a config edit alone. It needs the checkpoint
*served* (pushed to a private HF repo and the image rebuilt, or mounted from a
network volume with `NLI_MODEL` pointed at it); `passes: 1`, which only works on
`nli-runpod-bge-m3` **v0.4.0 or later** — earlier images silently drop the
parameter; `candidate_labels: ["SUPPORTS", "REFUTES", "NOT_ENOUGH_INFO"]`,
because `_direct_label_order()` matches by name against the model's own
`id2label` and `train_nli.py` writes exactly those three (the current
`["supports", "refutes", "is not relevant to"]` would fail every request with a
400); and a **full rescore**, since scored output is partitioned by
`scorer_config=<name>` and nothing carries over.

### What the split made worse

- **No single `tar_make()`.** Four projects run in order. Given that a bare
  `tar_make()` used to be able to spend RunPod GPU *and* OpenRouter money, this
  is closer to honesty than to loss.
- **Config targets are duplicated** across four preambles. Millisecond
  `yaml::read_yaml()` reads of one file; the cost is repetition, not compute.
- **Ordering is the operator's responsibility.** File hashing still catches a
  stale downstream, but nothing will *run* collection for you.
- **The big trees get hashed by producer and consumer both.**

## Pipeline DAG

This is the **logical** dependency chain end to end, as it was before the
split and as it still is in substance — it now spans three projects rather than
one (four until the `training` project was retired on 2026-10-05), with each consumer re-declaring the upstream outputs it reads as
`format = "file"` inputs under the producing project's own target names. The
per-project pictures above show where the cuts fall.

```
config_file (file)
    ├── sparql_url                              ← SPARQL backend string
    ├── purpose                                 ← this project's block (fact_checking: / training:)
    ├── scorer_name                              ← selected NLI profile name
    ├── scorer_config                              ← resolved NLI profile (host, model, etc.)
    ├── assessments_list
    │       └── assessment (list, branched)
    │               ├── ttl_path (file)                    ← Target 1
    │               ├── refs_sparql (file) ──────────────── queries/refs.sparql
    │               ├── refs_parquet (file)                ← Target 2a
    │               ├── key_messages_sparql (file) ──────── queries/key_messages.sparql
    │               ├── key_messages_parquet (file)        ← Target 2b2
    │               ├── zotero_parquet (file)              ← Target 2c
    │               ├── works_parquet (file)               ← Target 2d
    │               ├── snowball_parquet (file)            ← Target 2e
    │               └── works_citing_parquet (file)        ← Target 2f
    └── scorer_config ─────────────────────────────────────────┐
        assessment ─────────────────────────────────────────┤
        key_messages_parquet ───────────────────────────────┤→ nli_scores_parquet ← Target 2g
        works_citing_parquet ───────────────────────────────┘
```

**Phase 2 — LLM verification + candidate scoping** (both active targets):

```
assessment ───────────────────────────────────┐
key_messages_parquet ─────────────────────────┤
refs_parquet ──────────────────────────────────┤→ llm_candidate_scope_parquet ← Target 2h4a
works_parquet ─────────────────────────────────┤
snowball_parquet ──────────────────────────────┤
claim_work_pairs ────────────────────┘

scorer_name ──────────────────────────────────┐
assessment ──────────────────────────────────┤
claim_work_pairs ──────────────────┤
llm_verification_active ─────────────────────┤→ llm_verification_parquet ← Target 2h4b
llm_verification_config ─────────────────────┤
llm_verification_system_prompt_file ─────────┤
llm_verification_user_prompt_file ───────────┤
llm_candidate_scope_parquet ──────────────────┤
claim_scores_by_claim (DAG dep only) ──┘

config_file ── llm_verification_active ── llm_verification_config   (mirrors scorer_name → scorer_config)
```

`llm_candidate_scope_parquet` reads only already-existing, unmodified
targets (`key_messages_parquet`, `refs_parquet`, `works_parquet`,
`snowball_parquet`, `claim_completion_model`, plus `claim_work_pairs`
for a drift sanity check) — adding it does not invalidate Phase 1's NLI
chain or any download/snowball step upstream of it. Under
`naive_bm`/`complete_bm` it makes no network/API calls of its own; under
`atomic_bm` it re-runs `complete_bm_fragments()` (normally a cache-hit
against the completion cache a real atomic_bm `claim_work_pairs`
build already populated) to recover claim alignment. It always runs
regardless of which `llm_verification` config is active, since every
config's output now carries the `direct_evidence_match` tag it produces.

## Configuration (`input/config.yaml`)

```yaml
sparql_url: fuseki

assessments:
  - id: GA1
    ttl_url: https://...
  - id: IAS
    ttl_url: https://...

# `nli:` and `llm_verification:` are LIBRARIES of named definitions. They
# select nothing themselves -- see the purpose blocks below.
nli:
  configs:
    bge_m3_zeroshot_naive_bm:
      scheme: https
      host: ["<pod-id-1>-8080.proxy.runpod.net", "<pod-id-2>-8080.proxy.runpod.net"]
      port: null
      model: MoritzLaurer/bge-m3-zeroshot-v2.0-c   # deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0 was the original model, now retired
      candidate_labels: ["supports", "refutes", "is not relevant to"]
      hypothesis_template: "This paper {} the following claim: %s"
      batch_size: 64
      max_length: 2048
      uncertain_threshold: 0.60
      nei_threshold: 0.90
      granularity: naive_bm   # complete_bm / atomic_bm also supported

# Purpose blocks: scope + selection, one per consuming project.
fact_checking:
  assessments: [GA1]
  nli: bge_m3_zeroshot_atomic_bm
  llm: openrouter_cheap
  claim_completion: haiku_completion

training:
  assessments: [GA1, VA, TCA, IAS, BBA]
  nli: bge_m3_zeroshot_atomic_bm
  llm: openrouter_cheap
  claim_completion: haiku_completion
  finetune:
    enabled: true
    downsample_seed: 13
```

There is no global `active:` any more. It was a single answer to a question each
project answers for itself: fact checking is scoped to one assessment because it
is the expensive arm, while training pooled all five key-paper sets, and the two
need not have agreed on a model. While there was one DAG the conflation was
invisible; once the projects were split it was wrong. With `training` retired
there is again only one purpose block, but the mechanism is unchanged and the
hazard would return with any second one.

Selections are resolved and **validated** by `purpose_config()`
([R/branch_helpers.R](R/branch_helpers.R)) — naming a config that is not in the
corresponding library is a hard error, because it would otherwise read as
"nothing has been scored yet" and re-dispatch a corpus at real GPU cost.

Scope lives in the purpose block rather than as per-assessment flags inside
`assessments:`. Flags there would change `assessments_list`'s value and so
invalidate `assessment`, `ttl_path`, `works_parquet`, `snowball_parquet` and
everything downstream; `purpose_assessments_list()` preserves the exact element
shape `assessments_list` has always produced, so a purpose listing every
assessment yields a byte-identical value.

`train:`/`downsample_seed:` also moved out of the serving configs into
`training.finetune`, where they belong — how a model is *served* and whether the
training project *trains* one are different questions.

Config is split into fine-grained targets — each reads only its own section from
`config_file` directly (no intermediate `config` target). Changing one section
re-runs only that target; if the extracted value is unchanged, nothing downstream
cascades.

| Config key | Target | Invalidates |
|---|---|---|
| `sparql_url` | `sparql_url` | All SPARQL build targets |
| `assessments` | `assessments_list` → `assessment` | Assessment branches and their outputs |
| `fact_checking.*` / `training.*` | `purpose` (per project) → `scorer_name`, `llm_verification_active`, `claim_completion_model`, `assessments_list` | that project's chain only |
| `nli.configs.<selected>.*` | `scorer_config` | the NLI scoring chain of whichever project selected it |
| `llm_verification.configs.<selected>.*` | `llm_verification_config` | that project's LLM verification target only |

Note `config_file` is a `format = "file"` target over the **whole** YAML, so any
edit to it — including swapping a pod hostname — marks it outdated and
`tar_outdated()` projects that pessimistically down the chain. It clears itself
as soon as the cheap config targets re-run and produce identical values; nothing
expensive actually rebuilds.

## Target 0: `assessment` — Assessment Specs

**Source:** `_targets.R`

Creates a named list of assessment specifications from `assessments_list`. Each element gains an `index` field used for deterministic Fuseki port assignment. Branch names are the assessment IDs — adding a new assessment creates a new branch without invalidating existing ones.

## Target 1: `ttl_path` — Download TTL File

**Source:** `R/download_ttls.R` → `download_ttl(assessment)`

For each assessment branch:
1. Creates `output/LoD/` if it does not exist.
2. Queries the GitHub Contents API for the current SHA of the remote TTL file.
3. Skips the download if a local copy with a matching SHA already exists.
4. Otherwise downloads to `output/LoD/<id>.ttl` and writes the SHA next to it.

Returns a character vector of local TTL file paths (`format = "file"`).

> Even when `sparql_url` is a remote URL, TTL files are still downloaded as a declared pipeline dependency. The download is cheap once cached.

## Target 2a: `refs_parquet` — DB1

**Source:** `R/write_refs_parquet.R` → `build_refs_parquet(sparql_url, assessment, ttl_path, refs_sparql, "output/refs")`

Builds the refs dataset for one assessment branch and writes to `output/refs/assessment=<id>/`. When `sparql_url: fuseki`, starts a local Fuseki session, POSTs the TTL into the named graph, runs the SPARQL query, and stops Fuseki on exit.

### Reading DB1

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/refs") |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment == "GA1", km == "A.", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema — DB1

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier |
| `sm` | chr | Sub-Message identifier |
| `doi` | chr | DOI string — `NA` if absent |
| `description` | chr | Citation text from the LOD |
| `citation` | chr | Zotero-key citation string like `[P62TQUG2]` |
| `zotero_group` | chr | Zotero group id |
| `zotero_key` | chr | Raw Zotero item key |
| `zotero` | chr | Zotero URL (`owl:sameAs`) |

## Target 2b: `sections_parquet` — DB2 {.unnumbered}

## Disabled 2026-09-15 — no longer part of the pipeline

`sections_parquet` and `sections_sparql` are commented out in `_targets.R`, and
`output/sections/` has been deleted. Nothing consumed the dataset: no target
took `sections_parquet` as an argument and no `.qmd` read it — its only ever
consumer was `R/resolve_citations.R`, itself long orphaned — so it cost a SPARQL
extraction and Fuseki round trip per assessment on every rebuild for output
nothing read.

`R/write_sections_parquet.R` and `queries/sections.sparql` both still exist.
Re-enabling is uncommenting the block in `_targets.R`. The description below is
kept as a record of what it produced.
:::

**Source:** `R/write_sections_parquet.R` → `build_sections_parquet(sparql_url, assessment, ttl_path, sections_sparql, "output/sections")`

Built the sections dataset for one assessment branch. Each SubChapter source row carried the SubMessage that referenced it (`sm` column). Written to `output/sections/assessment=<id>/`.

### Reading DB2

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/sections") |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment == "GA1", km == "A.", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema — DB2

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier |
| `sm` | chr | Sub-Message identifier |
| `section` | chr | Chapter identifier |
| `subsection` | chr | SubChapter identifier |
| `content` | chr | SubChapter description text |

## Target 2b2: `key_messages_parquet` — DB3

**Source:** `R/write_key_messages_parquet.R` → `build_key_messages_parquet(sparql_url, assessment, ttl_path, key_messages_sparql, "output/key_messages")`

Builds the key/background/sub-messages dataset for one assessment branch. Written to `output/key_messages/assessment=<id>/`.

### Reading DB3

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/key_messages") |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment == "GA1", km == "A.", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema — DB3

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier |
| `km_label` | chr | KM headline text |
| `km_description` | chr | KM detail text |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier |
| `bm_label` | chr | BM headline text |
| `bm_description` | chr | BM detail text — used as NLI hypothesis |
| `bm_well_established` | chr | BM confidence flag |
| `bm_established_incomplete` | chr | BM confidence flag |
| `sm_id` | chr | Sub-Message identifier |
| `sm_description` | chr | SM statement text |
| `sm_well_established` | chr | SM confidence flag |
| `sm_established_incomplete` | chr | SM confidence flag |

## Target 2c: `zotero_parquet` — Zotero Group Items

**Source:** `R/download_zotero.R` → `download_zotero(assessment, refs_parquet)`

Reads the refs branch for one assessment, infers the Zotero group id from the `zotero` column, downloads all top-level Zotero items page by page, and writes to `output/zotero/assessment=<id>/` partitioned by `group_id` and `page`.

## Target 2d: `works_parquet` — OpenAlex Works

**Source:** `R/download_works.R` → `download_works(assessment, zotero_parquet, refs_parquet, workers = 8)`

Reads DOIs from the Zotero branch, fetches OpenAlex works with `openalexPro::pro_fetch()`, then joins with `refs_parquet` on normalised DOI to attach `km` and `bm` columns. Written to `output/works/assessment=<id>/` partitioned by `assessment`, `km`, and `bm`.

### Reading DB4

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/works") |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment == "GA1", km == "A.", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::select(id, doi, title) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema — DB4 (selected columns)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier (partition) |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier (partition) |
| `id` | chr | OpenAlex work ID URL |
| `doi` | chr | DOI string |
| `title` | chr | Work title |
| `publication_year` | int | Year of publication |
| … | … | 51 OpenAlex columns total |

## Target 2e: `snowball_parquet` — Snowball Search

**Source:** `R/build_snowball_parquet.R` → `build_snowball_parquet(assessment, works_parquet, "output/snowball")`

For each assessment branch, iterates over all km/bm combinations in `works_parquet` and calls `openalexSnowball::pro_snowball()` to retrieve all papers that cite or are cited by the seeds. Writes to three shared parquet roots:

- `output/snowball/nodes/` — partitioned by `assessment`, `km`, `bm`, `relation`
- `output/snowball/edges/` — partitioned by `assessment`, `km`, `bm`, `edge_type`
- `output/snowball/keypaper/` — partitioned by `assessment`, `km`, `bm`

### Reading

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/snowball/nodes") |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment == "GA1", km == "A.", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::select(id, doi, title, relation) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema — Nodes

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier (partition) |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier (partition) |
| `relation` | chr | `"keypaper"`, `"citing"`, or `"cited"` (partition) |
| `oa_input` | lgl | `TRUE` if this work was a seed |
| `id` | chr | OpenAlex work ID URL |
| `doi` | chr | DOI string |
| `title` | chr | Work title |
| `publication_year` | int | Year of publication |
| … | … | 53 columns total |

### Schema — Edges

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier (partition) |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier (partition) |
| `edge_type` | chr | `"core"`, `"extended"`, or `"outside"` (partition) |
| `from` | chr | OpenAlex ID of citing work |
| `to` | chr | OpenAlex ID of cited work |

## Target 2f: `works_citing_parquet` — Citing Works

**Source:** `R/build_works_citing_parquet.R` → `build_works_citing_parquet(assessment, snowball_parquet, "output/works_citing")`

Copies snowball nodes with `relation == "citing"` into `output/works_citing/assessment=<id>/km=<km>/bm=<bm>/`. File-copy approach is required because OpenAlex's nested struct columns can have inconsistent schemas across km/bm partitions.

### Reading

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/works_citing") |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment == "GA1", km == "A.", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::select(id, doi, title, publication_year) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema

Same columns as snowball nodes minus `relation` (always `citing` in this dataset).

## Target 2g: `nli_scores_parquet` — NLI Alignment Scores

**Source:** `R/build_nli_scores_parquet.R` → `build_nli_scores_parquet(assessment, key_messages_parquet, works_citing_parquet, scorer_config, scorer_name, "output/nli_scores")`

For each `(assessment, km, bm)` partition in `works_citing_parquet`:

1. Reads the BM description from `key_messages_parquet` as the NLI hypothesis.
2. Cleans each citing work's `title + abstract` as the premise.
3. POSTs batches to the zero-shot NLI server (see [external/runpod/docker/nli-runpod/](external/runpod/docker/nli-runpod/)).
4. Stores the full probability distribution (`p_supports`, `p_refutes`, `p_nei`) plus predicted label and confidence.

Output is written to `output/nli_scores/scorer_config=<cfg>/assessment=<id>/km=<km>/bm=<bm>/`, partitioned by `scorer_config` so scores from different model profiles are stored separately and comparable.

See [TD_BM_NLI_approach.qmd](TD_BM_NLI_approach.html) for full design rationale.

### Reading

```r
arrow::open_dataset("output/nli_scores") |>
  dplyr::filter(scorer_config == "deberta_zeroshot", assessment == "GA1", bm == "A1") |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

### Schema

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scorer_config` | chr | Active NLI profile name (partition) |
| `assessment` | chr | Assessment ID (partition) |
| `km` | chr | Key Message identifier (partition) |
| `bm` | chr | Background Message identifier (partition) |
| `work_id` | chr | OpenAlex work ID URL |
| `doi` | chr | DOI string |
| `title` | chr | Paper title |
| `publication_year` | int | Publication year |
| `label` | chr | Predicted label: `SUPPORTS`, `REFUTES`, or `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` |
| `p_supports` | dbl | Model probability for SUPPORTS |
| `p_refutes` | dbl | Model probability for REFUTES |
| `p_nei` | dbl | Model probability for NOT_ENOUGH_INFO |
| `confidence` | dbl | `max(p_supports, p_refutes, p_nei)` |
| `uncertain` | lgl | `TRUE` if `confidence < uncertain_threshold` |

## Target 2h4a: `llm_candidate_scope_parquet` — per-claim evidence match set

**Source:** `R/build_llm_candidate_scope_parquet.R`

Chains `refs_parquet`'s `sm` (sub-chapter id) → seed doi → seed OpenAlex
work id → citing work (via the existing snowball edges) to produce, per
claim, the set of citing works tied to that claim's own evidentiary
sub-chapter rather than the whole BM's — `llm_verification_parquet` tags
every reviewed pair `direct_evidence_match` against this set (formerly used
to *filter* candidates via a `subset: "default"` config setting; retired
once real GA1 atomic_bm data showed the narrowing reduced routed pairs by
only ~14%, not worth the lost review coverage — see
[TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.qmd](TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.html#candidate-scoping)).
Supported for `naive_bm`/`atomic_bm`; a no-op sentinel for `complete_bm`
(no per-sub-claim evidence tokens exist for whole-field claims — every row
is tagged FALSE there). Reads only already-existing, unmodified targets
(`key_messages_parquet`, `refs_parquet`, `works_parquet`, `snowball_parquet`,
`claim_completion_model`, and `claim_work_pairs` for a drift
sanity check); under `naive_bm`/`complete_bm` makes no network/API calls of
its own, but under `atomic_bm` re-runs `complete_bm_fragments()` (normally a
cache-hit against the completion cache already populated by a real
`claim_work_pairs` atomic_bm build) to recover which fragments
survived completion. Deliberately does **not** call `segment_bm_by_evidence()`
or `segment_bm_atomic()` (`R/build_claim_work_pairs.R`) — even a
behavior-preserving edit there would mark `claim_work_pairs`, and
the NLI scoring chain downstream of it, outdated, since `targets` hashes
function bodies as dependencies. Instead duplicates the small amount of
segmentation logic needed for each, verified byte-for-byte identical in
behavior against the originals. See
[TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.qmd](TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.html#candidate-scoping) for
the full design, including the fallback and prefix-matching policy
decisions. Writes to
`output/llm_candidate_scope/assessment=<id>/km=<km>/bm=<bm>/`
(`assessment, km, bm, claim_id, work_id` — one row per matched pair).
Always computed regardless of which `llm_verification` config is active.

## Target 2h4b: `llm_verification_parquet` — Phase 2 LLM verification

**Source:** `R/build_llm_verification_parquet.R`

One `ellmer::chat_openrouter()` call per `(claim, work)` pair selected by
the active config's `nli_labels`/`nli_certainty` fields (see
[TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.qmd](TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.html) for the full design
and its ported-architecture rationale) — `select_llm_verification_candidates()`
filters on `label %in% nli_labels` AND the certainty band, both optional
(`NULL`/absent = no filter on that dimension); currently every shipped
config sets `nli_labels: [REFUTES, SUPPORTS]`, `nli_certainty: certain`.
Every selected candidate is reviewed — none are filtered further —
but `tag_direct_evidence_match()` tags each one against
`llm_candidate_scope_parquet` (see
[TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.qmd](TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.html#candidate-scoping) for
why this used to be a filter and no longer is).
Resumable per-`(km, bm, claim_id, work_id)` JSON cache under
`output/llm_verification/raw/model=<model>/prompt=<hash>/assessment=<id>/`
— keyed on the full 4-part identity, not `claim_id`+`work_id` alone, for
the same reason `tag_direct_evidence_match()` above matches on the full
`(km, bm, claim_id, work_id)` key rather than `claim_id` alone; final output —
`nli_label`, `llm_label`, `llm_agrees`, `direct_evidence_match`, a required
verbatim `quote` (demoted to `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` if fabricated), `explanation`
— written to
`output/llm_verification/scores/llm_config=<config>/assessment=<id>/nli_route=<route>/km=<km>/bm=<bm>/`.
`nli_route` is `nli_route_label()`'s hive-safe encoding of **that row's
own** NLI outcome (e.g. `REFUTES-certain`), computed per row from its
actual label/uncertain values — not a single value per config call, so a
config listing several labels/certainties (e.g. `nli_labels: [REFUTES, SUPPORTS]`)
still writes one `nli_route=` subdirectory per distinct outcome actually
present, never a merged string. `llm_config`/`assessment` form the
fixed prefix fully deleted and rewritten each call.

Configured via `input/config.yaml`'s `llm_verification:` block — a library of
named `configs` (`model`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `max_active`,
`max_retries`, `nli_labels`, `nli_certainty` per config), mirroring `nli:`'s
structure exactly. Which one a project uses comes from its purpose block's
`llm:` field, not from an `active:` key. Three configs ship by default
(`openrouter_cheap`/`openrouter_midtier`/`openrouter_toptier_gpt5` — a
fourth, `openrouter_cheap_sm`, was removed once `subset` itself was retired,
since it differed from `openrouter_cheap` only by that setting), the model
tiers carried over from the sibling `Categorisation_Literature` project's
`epistemology:` config, including its proven `max_active: 24`/`max_tokens: 8000`
values. This replaced an earlier truth/citing-document LLM design
(`prompts_truth_parquet` → `prompts_citing_parquet` →
`alignement_scores_parquet`, driven by an `analysis:` config block) — all
of that source has been removed; see [TD_LLM_approach.qmd](TD_LLM_approach.html)
for why.

## Target 2h4b' (QA, key papers): `llm_verification_keypaper_parquet` — full-coverage key-paper LLM verification

**Source:** `R/build_llm_verification_keypaper_parquet.R`

QA sanity check, **not** the main Phase 2 corpus — mirrors
`claim_scores_keypaper`'s own relationship to the main NLI chain.
Reviews **every** key/seed paper's NLI-scored pair, irrespective of
`nli_labels`/`nli_certainty` — unlike `llm_verification_parquet` above,
which routes by those fields purely for cost control on a millions-of-rows
corpus, key papers are a small, bounded, high-importance set (the actual
evidence a BM was written from) where every one is worth an independent
check. Structural sibling of `build_llm_verification_parquet()`, same
"separate file, don't touch the delicate already-working builder"
precedent `R/build_claim_work_pairs_keypaper.R` already documents
for its own Phase-1 counterpart — doubly justified here since that
function was only just stabilized against a `pair_id` collision bug (fixed
in the same turn this chain was added) and shouldn't be touched again for
an unrelated variant.

Reuses directly (calls, does not duplicate) the small generic helpers
already in `build_llm_verification_parquet.R` —
`build_llm_verification_chat()`, `llm_verification_output_type()`,
`normalise_llm_verification()`, `quote_is_verbatim()`, `render_template()`,
`load_text_file()`, `nli_route_label()`, and critically
`select_llm_verification_candidates()` itself, which is already fully
path-parameterized (not hardcoded to the citing-works tree) and already
supports "no filter" via `nli_labels = NULL, nli_certainty = NULL` —
exactly what full coverage needs, with no changes to that function
required. Does duplicate the chunking/`run_pairs()`/retry/cache-write/
output-assembly orchestration loop, adapted to the keypaper paths. No
`direct_evidence_match` tagging — that concept (does a *citing* work trace
back to a seed reference matching the claim's evidence braces) doesn't
apply to a key paper, which *is* a seed reference itself; the column is
omitted from this chain's output schema entirely rather than a meaningless
always-FALSE/NA placeholder.

Reads premise from `claim_work_pairs_keypaper`'s own
per-assessment path and NLI scores from
`output/nli_scores_evidence_keypaper/granularity=<g>/scorer_config=<cfg>/assessment=<id>/`.
Writes to its own `output/llm_verification/scores_keypaper/` root (cache
under `output/llm_verification/raw_keypaper/`) — never collides with or
invalidates the main citing-works output tree. Takes
`claim_scores_keypaper` as a bare (DAG-dependency-only) argument,
same convention `llm_verification_parquet` already uses for
`claim_scores_by_claim` — runs automatically as part of a bare
`tar_make()`.

**New paid API surface**, same caution as `llm_verification_parquet` and
`claim_scores_keypaper` themselves: a plain `tar_make()`/
`tar_make(names = "report_fact_checker")` now also dispatches real
OpenRouter calls for every key paper, not just the routed citing-works
subset. Use `tar_make(names = ..., shortcut = TRUE)` to render against
on-disk data without triggering a fresh run.

## Target 2h4b'' (QA data/figures): `llm_verification_qa_data`, `llm_verification_qa_figures` — Phase 2 QA report

**Source:** `R/build_llm_verification_qa_data.R`, `R/build_llm_verification_qa_figures.R`

Sibling to `nli_scores_qa_data`/`nli_scores_qa_figures` (which QA Phase 1).
Single-active-granularity, **not** `cross()`'d over `nli_granularities` —
`llm_verification_parquet` only ever reflects whichever granularity is
currently active, so there's nothing to cross here either.
`llm_verification_parquet`'s own output already carries everything needed
per row (no re-join of Phase 1's scored table needed); only
`title`/`abstract`/`doi` get joined in, from `works_citing_parquet` for
citing works and from `works_parquet` for key papers (a distinct lookup
path — key papers are SEED works, not in the citing-works dataset).

Computes an `nli_label` × `llm_label` contingency once (`label_flow`),
reused both for the report's confusion-matrix table and as Figure 2's
direct input, plus a per-NLI-confidence-decile `llm_agrees` rate (Figure
1's input) and, when `llm_verification_keypaper_parquet` has data, the
key-paper validation fields (`keypaper_n`, `keypaper_llm_supports_pct`,
`keypaper_llm_agrees_pct`, and an **uncapped**
`keypaper_flagged_widget` DT table of every key paper the LLM did *not*
confirm as SUPPORTS — key papers are a bounded, small set, so unlike the
main claims table there's no `per_claim_cap` need here).

**A literal ternary plot (Phase 1's own QA figure) was considered and
rejected** for Phase 2: the LLM emits one categorical verdict, not a
3-part probability composition, so a simplex density would really just be
NLI's own chart wearing a Phase-2 label. Two figures instead, in a new
file — deliberately does **not** modify `R/build_claim_scores_qa_figures.R`/
`claim_scores_qa_ternary_plot()`, same "duplicate, don't call" discipline
protecting Phase-1-adjacent (explicitly locked) code from unrelated
invalidation:

1. `llm_verification_qa_decile_plot()` — X = NLI-confidence decile, Y = %
   of reviewed pairs where `llm_agrees`, one line (point size = n). Key
   papers overlay the **same** `llm_agrees` metric — individual jittered
   points at each key paper's own confidence, plus a dashed aggregate
   reference line — so the two series are directly comparable on one
   y-axis; the "% confirmed SUPPORTS" framing is deliberately kept out of
   this chart's own metric and lives in the report's plain-text summary
   bullets instead.
2. `llm_verification_qa_alluvial_plot()` — an `nli_label` → `llm_label`
   flow diagram (`ggalluvial::geom_alluvium()`/`geom_stratum()`, a **new
   dependency** — already installed but not previously referenced in this
   project; no `renv.lock`/`DESCRIPTION` exists here to update) coloured
   by agreement, with key papers shown as a **side-by-side mini-alluvial**
   (`patchwork::wrap_plots()`, also new) rather than an overlaid second
   flow, since key-paper `n` is typically orders of magnitude smaller than
   the full reviewed corpus and would be visually invisible on the main
   flow's scale.

Empty-state guard checks `dir.exists()` **and** that the path actually
contains `.parquet` files (same pattern `tag_direct_evidence_match()`
uses), not `dir.exists()` alone, since `llm_verification_parquet`/
`llm_verification_keypaper_parquet` can return their `output_path` even
when nothing was written. Rendered via `QA_LLM_Verification_Report.qmd`
(`llm_verification_qa_report_html` target), filename
`QA_LLM_Verification_Report_<assessment>_<llm_config>.html` (`llm_config`
always suffixed — no unsuffixed-default exception, unlike
`nli_model_suffix()`'s historical one for `"deberta_zeroshot"`).

## Target 2h4c: `{refutes,supports}_funnel_{data,figures,tables}` — label funnels

**Source:** `R/build_label_funnel_data.R`, `R/build_label_funnel_figures.R`, `R/build_label_funnel_tables.R`

A 3-level sieve of distinct citing works per `(km, bm)`, each level a subset
of the previous: (1) the snowball corpus (`works_citing_parquet`), (2) NLI
`<label>` + certain (`nli_scores_evidence`), (3) of those, `llm_agrees ==
TRUE` in `llm_verification_parquet` (re-filtered to `nli_route ==
paste0(target_label, "-certain")` defensively, in case a future config
routes other outcomes into the same output tree). A 4th level,
`sufficient_evidence == TRUE`, was considered for the original REFUTES-only
version and dropped: `build_llm_verification_parquet.R`'s own parser forces
`llm_label` to `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` whenever `sufficient_evidence` is `FALSE`,
so `llm_agrees == TRUE` already implies `sufficient_evidence == TRUE` for
every row — a 4th level would always equal the 3rd, never narrowing
anything further.

`build_label_funnel_data(assessment, target_label, ..., granularity)` is
one shared implementation called twice from `_targets.R` — once with
`target_label = "REFUTES"` (target `refutes_funnel_data`), once with
`"SUPPORTS"` (target `supports_funnel_data`) — rather than two
near-identical copies. Each branches over `pattern = cross(map(assessment,
works_citing_parquet, llm_verification_parquet), nli_granularities)` — a
combinatorial product against a fixed `nli_granularities <- c("naive_bm",
"complete_bm")` (not read from config; both are always rendered, one
falling back to the empty-data state until a `complete_bm` NLI config is
actually run), NOT a plain `map()`, since `nli_granularities` is an
independent dimension from `assessment`, not zipped 1:1 with it — 4
branches per target (2 assessments x 2 granularities), not 2. Downstream
`refutes_funnel_figures`/`refutes_funnel_tables`/`report_refutes_funnel_html`
only need a plain `pattern = map(refutes_funnel_data, ...)` (and similarly
for `supports_*`) since they consume already-4-branched siblings from the
same `cross()`, all in the same order — no re-crossing needed downstream.
`report_refutes_funnel_html`/`report_supports_funnel_html` deliberately do
NOT include `assessment` in their own pattern (it only has 2 branches,
which would mismatch the 4-branched funnel data/figures/tables) — instead
they read `assessment`/`granularity` back out of the funnel data rds
itself (both stored there), which stays correctly aligned with whichever
branch is executing.

Each branch depends only on `works_citing_parquet`, `scorer_name` (to
reconstruct the `nli_scores_evidence` path, same convention as
`nli_overview_data`'s call site, with a `granularity=<value>/` segment
inserted using the branch's OWN `nli_granularities` value, not the single
active-config one), and `llm_verification_parquet` — pure local
`arrow`/`dplyr`, no network/GPU calls, and no edge into
`claim_scores_by_claim`'s actual computation (only as an
already-built dependency elsewhere in the pipeline). Reuses
`build_claim_scores_overview_data.R`'s doi-lookup join verbatim, since neither
source table stores `doi`. `deployment = "main"` for the same OOM reason as
`nli_overview_data` (a full per-assessment `nli_scores_evidence` collect()).
`nli_overview_data`/`nli_overview_figures`/`nli_bm_explorer_html` (not
otherwise covered by this stale document — see the note at the top) went
through the identical `cross()` treatment for the same reason.

`build_label_funnel_figures()` renders three PNGs per assessment (overall
funnel, per-BM grouped bars, and a normalized per-BM variant where each
level is divided by that BM's own corpus count so it reads 1 — lets BMs be
compared on conversion rate regardless of raw corpus size).
`build_label_funnel_tables()` renders one `DT::datatable()` table (level 3)
with a BM dropdown filter — see [output/README.md](../output/README.md)'s
Details section for the exact column-curation rationale (bypasses
`IPBES.R::table_dt()`, since its wrapper can't pass through DT's top-level
`filter` argument).

Rendered into standalone reports parameterized by both assessment and label.
**This section describes the pre-2026-09-18 design and is kept for the
record; see `CLAUDE.md`'s "Quarto Report" section for what the pipeline does
now.** Formerly: `IPBES_Label_Funnel_Report.qmd` →
`report_refutes_funnel_html`/`report_supports_funnel_html` via Quarto's
`params:`/`execute_params=`, with the qmd resolving which label's data to
read through `targets::tar_read_raw()` keyed off `params$label`.

Today all reports live in one Quarto project (`input/reports/_quarto.yml`)
rendered by `tarchetypes::tar_quarto()`. Because a project renders each
`.qmd` exactly once, the parameterized families became a shared body
(`_IPBES_Label_Funnel_Report_body.qmd`) plus one generated wrapper per
combination, written from `config.yaml`'s `reports:` section by
`generate_report_wrappers()`. `tar_read_raw()` is gone: it was invisible to
`tarchetypes`, so these reports contributed no dependency edges at all and
each render target had to fake them with bare symbol references.

`SUPPORTS` was added to every `llm_verification` config's `nli_labels`
(`input/config.yaml`) at the same time the SUPPORTS funnel report was
added, so Phase 2 now reviews both labels' certain pairs — see
`TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.qmd`'s cost table for the measured pair counts.

---

## SPARQL Queries

The SPARQL queries live in `queries/*.sparql` and are tracked as `format = "file"` targets. Changing a query file invalidates only the downstream parquet target.

| File | Target | Traversal |
|---|---|---|
| `queries/refs.sparql` | `refs_parquet` | `KM → BM → SM → SubChapter ← Reference(doi)` |
| `queries/sections.sparql` | *(none — `sections_parquet` disabled)* | `KM → BM → SM → SubChapter(content) → Chapter` (projects `sm_id`) |
| `queries/key_messages.sparql` | `key_messages_parquet` | `KM → BM → SM` (text + confidence flags) |

All queries wrap their pattern in `GRAPH <%GRAPH_IRI%> { ... }`. The placeholder
is substituted at query time by `read_sparql_query()` using `assessment_graph_iri()`
from `R/branch_helpers.R` — currently `http://ontology.ipbes.net/report/<id>`.
Switching backends is a one-line change in `input/config.yaml` (`sparql_url:`).

## Orphaned / Deprecated Source Files

Not wired into the current `_targets.R`; kept for reference:

- `R/build_fulltext.R` — legacy Grobid XML / PDF download for citing works
- `R/resolve_citations.R` — replace `(Author, Year)` with OpenAlex W-IDs in section content

## Notes

- All parquet targets are assessment-branched; there is no cached combined object.
- Each assessment branch rewrites only its own partition directory.
- Credentials (`API_openalex`, `API_openrouter`) are read from the macOS keyring by `_targets.R` at session start via `keyring::key_get()`.

## Required R Packages

| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| `targets` | Pipeline engine |
| `yaml` | Config parsing |
| `keyring` | API credential retrieval |
| `processx` | Fuseki subprocess management |
| `httr2` | HTTP SPARQL queries, Graph Store Protocol POSTs, NLI server requests |
| `readr` | CSV response parsing |
| `arrow` | Parquet I/O |
| `dplyr` | Data manipulation |
| `tictoc` | Query timing |
| `jsonlite` | JSON serialisation for prompts |
| `xml2`, `stringr` | Text cleaning (`clean_text.R`) |
| `ellmer` | OpenRouter chat client (parked LLM chain) |
| `openalexPro` | OpenAlex works download |
| `openalexSnowball` | Snowball search |
| `future`, `future.apply` | Parallel workers |

**System dependency:** `fuseki-server` on `PATH` (install with `brew install fuseki`). Only required when `sparql_url: fuseki`.
